Q: Counting rows in left joined table A:

Just change the query to this - 

SELECT u.id, u.email, u.salt, u.pass, u.approved, 
u.ban, SUM(u2.status) AS status FROM `users` AS u 
LEFT JOIN `log` AS u2 ON u2.user_id = u.id 
WHERE u.email = ?
GROUP BY u.id

There are a number of other ways to do this as well.

Q: Errors in running the Clash interpreter A:

I was missing an import for the ncurses library, as described from the below snippet from my console output:

hint                     > ld: library not found for -lncurses

so I just had to add pkgs.ncurses to my shell.nix file, like so:

{ pkgs ? import <nixpkgs> { system = "x86_64-darwin"; } }:

pkgs.mkShell {
  buildInputs = [
    pkgs.stack

    # required for clashi
    pkgs.libiconv
    pkgs.libffi
    pkgs.ncurses  ##### <- add import here! #####
  ];
}

thanks @Noughtmare!

Q: DPI-1047: Cannot locate a 64-bit Oracle Client library: "The specified module could not be found" - Not Duplicate A:

To expand on some of the comments:

  • Give us more detail so we know what you are trying to do. In particular is your DB remote or on the same computer? This will determine whether you need Instant Client

  • The installation instructions for Windows are https://cx-oracle.readthedocs.io/en/latest/user_guide/installation.html#installing-cx-oracle-on-windows

  • use Instant Client 19.6 because this can connect to the same range of DB versions that Instant Client 12 can. But it has more features and fixes.

  • Make sure you have the correct Windows VS redistributable installed. This is a common problem.

  • Depending how you set PATH, you may need to restart a terminal window to get the updated value. Show us what you have set PATH to. Note that with cx_Oracle 8 on Windws, you could use init_oracle_client() instead of setting PATH, but you would need to call it in every python script. The usage is shown in the doc.

Q: Converting to Date Time Using as.POSIXct A:

So some comments first. When you read strings in R, unless you specify otherwise they are imported as factors. You can use the Option

Trying what @Disco Superfly has suggested works if you define the data as a string in R

> a <- "2016-12-05-16.25.54.875000"
> as.POSIXct(a, format="%Y-%m-%d-%H.%M.%S") 
[1] "2016-12-05 16:25:54 CET"
> as.POSIXct(a)
[1] "2016-12-05 CET"

Is not clear what you are saying about the fact that the data is being changed. Can you give a reproducible example?

To summarize, if your Dates are strings that what other have already suggested works perfectly. I suppose you are trying to do more than what you are explaining and therefore I don't understand what you are saying exactly.
